message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"12.12","text":"After Peter had said this, one of our company dared to speak for everyone and urged him to sail earlier the next morning to Aradus, the island opposite, which I think was not even a full thirty stadia away, to view the two vinewood columns there, which were of enormous thickness. Peter, being accommodating, agreed and said, “When you disembark from the ship, do not go in all at once as a large group to see the things you desire. I do not want the citizens turning toward us.” So we sailed and, in a fraction of an hour, put in at the island. After getting out of the boat, we went in to where the vinewood columns stood; and at the same time, together with them, one person viewed one of Phidias’s works and another a different one.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"εἷς τις τῶν ἐν ἡμῖν τολμήσας ἀντὶ πάντων","chosen":"one of our company dared to speak for everyone","rationale":"The act supplied by τολμήσας is implicit; speaking is supported by the following request, while ἀντὶ πάντων means on behalf of all."},{"source_quote":"ὡς ἐπὶ ἱστορίᾳ","chosen":"to view","rationale":"ἱστορία here denotes inspection or sightseeing, not the writing of history."},{"source_quote":"τῶν ἐκεῖ ἀμπελίων δύο στύλων","chosen":"the two vinewood columns there","rationale":"The supplied print reads ἀμπελίων, not the genitive plural ἀμπελίνων expected if ἀμπέλινος directly modified στύλων. The later wording οἱ ἀμπέλινοι στύλοι identifies the same columns as vinewood or vine-related and therefore supports the contextual rendering “vinewood columns.” A possible normalization is disclosed in source_issues but is not substituted for the selected reading."},{"source_quote":"οὐ γὰρ βούλομαι στρέμματα γίνεσθαι εἰς ἡμᾶς τῶν πολιτῶν","chosen":"I do not want the citizens turning toward us","rationale":"The source-transparent wording treats στρέμματα as turnings directed toward the visitors. In context this may mean attracting the citizens’ attention or causing them to turn and look; “the citizens turning against us,” implying hostility or disturbance, is also possible but is not required by the noun itself."},{"source_quote":"ῥοπῇ ὥρας","chosen":"in a fraction of an hour","rationale":"ῥοπή can denote a brief turn or moment; the phrase indicates a short portion of an hour, with “in a moment” also possible."},{"source_quote":"ὁμῶς ἅμα αὐτοῖς ἄλλος ἄλλο τι τῶν Φειδίου ἔργων ἐθεώρει","chosen":"at the same time, together with them, one person viewed one of Phidias’s works and another a different one","rationale":"The distributive ἄλλος ἄλλο τι is explicit. The referent of αὐτοῖς may be the columns or other members of the party, so the English pronoun preserves that ambiguity."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἀμπελίων","issue":"The selected edition prints ἀμπελίων. If the intended construction was an adjective directly modifying στύλων, the expected genitive plural of ἀμπέλινος would be ἀμπελίνων. The printed form might instead be construed as a genitive plural referring to vines or vineyards, but the later οἱ ἀμπέλινοι στύλοι supports the contextual sense “vinewood columns.” The selected reading remains unchanged, and the uncertainty does not prevent a defensible translation.","proposed_reading":"ἀμπελίνων (conjectural normalization only)","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
